headline: Bangladesh and US sign civil nuclear cooperation deal for peaceful energy
summary: The agreement aims to deepen ties on the peaceful use of nuclear energy to strengthen long-term energy security for both nations.
details: Bangladesh and the United States have signed a memorandum of understanding (MoU) on strategic civil nuclear cooperation to deepen ties on the peaceful use of nuclear energy.

The deal was signed on September 25 in New York by Rehan Asad, adviser to the prime minister for telecom and ICT, and Jacob Helberg, US under secretary of state for economic growth, energy, and the environment.

Both nations recognized the strategic significance of their diplomatic relationship and the role nuclear energy can play in meeting energy requirements and enhancing regional and international security.
The MoU emphasizes that all civil nuclear cooperation must follow the highest standards of nuclear safety, security, safeguards, and non-proliferation.
Both countries are parties to the Treaty on the Non-Proliferation of Nuclear Weapons (NPT) and have International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) safeguards agreements and additional protocols in force.
This development comes as Bangladesh seeks to diversify its long-term energy sources, having already built its first nuclear power plant at Rooppur.
In May, the two countries also signed another MoU on strategic cooperation in the broader energy sector to further strengthen energy security through diversified sourcing.
caption:
Bangladesh and the US have officially partnered for the peaceful use of nuclear energy.

Bangladesh and the United States have signed a memorandum of understanding (MoU) on strategic civil nuclear cooperation to deepen ties on the peaceful use of nuclear energy.

The deal was signed on September 25 in New York by Rehan Asad, adviser to the prime minister for telecom and ICT, and Jacob Helberg, US under secretary of state for economic growth, energy, and the environment.

Both nations recognized the strategic significance of their diplomatic relationship and the role nuclear energy can play in meeting energy requirements and enhancing regional and international security.

The MoU emphasizes that all civil nuclear cooperation must follow the highest standards of nuclear safety, security, safeguards, and non-proliferation.

Both countries are parties to the Treaty on the Non-Proliferation of Nuclear Weapons (NPT) and have International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) safeguards agreements and additional protocols in force.

This development comes as Bangladesh seeks to diversify its long-term energy sources, having already built its first nuclear power plant at Rooppur.

In May, the two countries also signed another MoU on strategic cooperation in the broader energy sector to further strengthen energy security through diversified sourcing.

headline_marked: 3.4mn children target: [[Govt launches nationwide measles-rubella vaccination]]
headline: 3.4mn children target: Govt launches nationwide measles-rubella vaccination
summary: The special catch-up drive aims to reach 2.4 million children who missed previous rounds to contain an ongoing outbreak.
details: Bangladesh has launched a nationwide special vaccination campaign to contain a measles outbreak, targeting 3.4 million children aged six to 59 months.
Health Minister Sardar Md Sakhawat Husain announced that the drive includes 1 million infants who recently reached six months of age and 2.4 million children who previously missed their vaccinations.
The 'Intensified MR Catch-up Vaccination' campaign will run until October 31, with centers operating seven days a week, including evening services for working mothers.
UNICEF has supplied 4.3 million vaccine doses to support the effort, emphasizing the urgency after nearly 1,000 lives were lost in the recent outbreak.
Health workers are tasked with vaccinating over 100,000 children per day to meet the target within the 36-day window.
Joint monitoring teams from the WHO, UNICEF, and the health ministry will conduct field reviews across all eight divisions from October 4 to 14 to assess surveillance systems.
Health Services Division Secretary ANM Bazlur Rashid stated that reaching this target is critical for establishing herd immunity and eliminating measles and rubella from the country.
caption:
Nearly 1,000 lives lost to measles. Now, the government is racing to vaccinate 3.4 million children to stop the outbreak.

Bangladesh has launched a nationwide special vaccination campaign to contain a measles outbreak, targeting 3.4 million children aged six to 59 months.

Health Minister Sardar Md Sakhawat Husain announced that the drive includes 1 million infants who recently reached six months of age and 2.4 million children who previously missed their vaccinations.

The 'Intensified MR Catch-up Vaccination' campaign will run until October 31, with centers operating seven days a week, including evening services for working mothers.

UNICEF has supplied 4.3 million vaccine doses to support the effort, emphasizing the urgency after nearly 1,000 lives were lost in the recent outbreak.

Health workers are tasked with vaccinating over 100,000 children per day to meet the target within the 36-day window.

Joint monitoring teams from the WHO, UNICEF, and the health ministry will conduct field reviews across all eight divisions from October 4 to 14 to assess surveillance systems.

Health Services Division Secretary ANM Bazlur Rashid stated that reaching this target is critical for establishing herd immunity and eliminating measles and rubella from the country.
